name: Sports
blurb: Performance analytics, broadcast automation, and officiating assistance, from NCAA and NFHS governance to Hudl, Catapult, and the sports technology research network.

points.desc: Census BTOS covers arts, entertainment, and recreation in its AI-use series.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: College sports' governing body is where AI questions about recruiting, roster management, and transfer analytics get policy answers.
points.name: The NCAA governs the college layer

points.desc: The National Federation of State High School Associations monitors scholastic sports tech - safety equipment, automated streaming, and recruiting policy for 12,000+ member schools.
points.name: NFHS covers high school sports technology

points.desc: The Sports & Fitness Industry Association publishes participation and equipment-market research covering technology adoption in youth and scholastic sports.
points.name: SFIA tracks the market data

points.desc: The dominant platform for game film across high school, college, and pro programs - its computer-vision scouting and automated capture cameras are the de facto standard for how AI reaches the sideline.
points.name: Hudl sets the video-analysis standard

points.name: Catapult and Kinexon instrument the athletes

summary: Performance analytics, broadcast automation, and officiating assistance are the visible deployments. Coverage of who tracks the sector runs from the governing bodies down to the platforms whose tooling sets the de facto standards.

analysis.body:
Per Census BTOS, the latest AI-use figure for arts, entertainment, and recreation (NAICS 71), the broad sector that includes sports, is 20.0%, and the prior period figure is 16.6%. The survey asks whether a business used AI in the last two weeks. This is a sector-wide measure, not a sports-only figure.

Per Hudl, AI-powered Focus cameras provide hands-free capture of game film for player development, livestreams, and highlights, and its trackers and AI-powered intelligence platform support recovery and performance metrics, including team averages, scatterplots, and AI chat. Catapult describes its platform as sports technology, data analytics, and insights. Catapult and Kinexon are identified as the primary wearable and tracking platforms for biomechanics and load management in NCAA and professional leagues, where athlete-monitoring AI runs.

Hudl is described as the dominant platform for game film across high school, college, and pro programs, and its computer-vision scouting and automated capture cameras are the de facto standard for how AI reaches the sideline. Catapult and Kinexon hold the primary position in wearable and tracking platforms. The cited pages do not provide revenue or investment figures, so the money side of this concentration is not quantified.

None of the cited sources report ROI evidence such as cost savings, revenue gains, or performance improvements tied to AI deployment. SFIA's research covers participation and equipment-market data, including technology adoption in youth and scholastic sports, but the excerpt does not give AI-specific return figures. STRN emphasizes bringing trustworthy and effective sports technology to market based on science, but again without ROI numbers.

Per NCAA, the college layer is governed across 1,000+ member schools and three divisions, and AI questions about recruiting, roster management, and transfer analytics get policy answers there. Per NFHS, high school sports rules are updated annually to minimize risk and ensure fair play, and the federation offers fully automated streaming equipment with no staffing required. NFHS monitors scholastic sports tech, safety equipment, automated streaming, and recruiting policy for 12,000+ member schools. STRN, a nonprofit initiative of Ghent University's Victoris consortium with SportaMundi, has published a peer-reviewed quality framework for assessing sports tech.

A reader deciding whether to deploy should note that measured adoption in the broad arts, entertainment, and recreation sector is 20.0%, with the prior period at 16.6%, and that AI is already embedded in video analysis and athlete monitoring through established vendors. Governance and quality frameworks exist at the NCAA, NFHS, and STRN levels, but the cited material does not provide ROI evidence, so any deployment decision would need to be tested against specific use cases and the relevant rules.

https://sfia.org/.brief: SFIA released a 2026 report examining participation across 30 sports, analyzing why people engage in team sports and how costs affect participation rates. The organization also published 92 single-sport reports providing five-year participation trends broken down by demographic factors including gender, age, education, geography, income, and ethnicity, plus cross-participation data with other activities. These reports are positioned as early indicators to help industry leaders plan for 2025 trends.

https://www.hudl.com/.brief: Hudl claims its sports technology software, video capture and data insights help athletes, coaches, teams and organizations win at every level. The company says its AI-powered Focus cameras provide “hands-free, hassle-free capture” of every moment, producing HD film for player development, livestreams and highlights. Hudl also offers visual representations of athlete performance metrics, including team averages, scatterplots, AI chat and tracking data. Additionally, the platform’s trackers and AI-powered intelligence are said to help players recover faster and compete at their best.

https://www.ncaa.org/.brief: The NCAA.org homepage presents the NCAA as the official athletics website that supports student-athletes, member schools, and championships across more than 1,000 schools in all three divisions. It explains that college sports are “nothing less than the world’s greatest tool for human development” and that the organization offers support, opportunity, and resources beyond the school environment. The site highlights its governance, trusted standards, and championships as ways to serve student-athletes at every level. It also notes that the website uses cookies and Cloudflare bot-management cookies to improve performance and protect against automated traffic.

https://www.nfhs.org/.brief: The NFHS sets and maintains rules for high school sports in the United States and provides resources focused on health, safety, leadership, and participation. Its site features participation statistics, a parent perspective study, a national record book, and advocacy for middle school athletics. The organization reports that 9 out of 10 music educators entered the profession to find purpose. It also offers digital access to rules, officials and coaches associations, and a streaming service for school events, with the stated goal of letting all students “Play, Perform and Compete Together.”
